definitions.explanation: A steep rock face, especially at the edge of the sea or a mountain.

examples.japanese: {崖|がけ}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{落|お}ちそうになった→落ちる：01242_ochiru⟧。
examples.english: I almost fell off the cliff.

examples.japanese: {崖|がけ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{上|うえ}→上：00682_ue⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{景色|けしき}→景色：01395_keshiki⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{絶景|ぜっけい}→絶景：16835_zekkei⟧⟦だった→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: The view from the top of the cliff was spectacular.

examples.japanese: ⟦{崖崩|がけくず}れ→崖崩れ：20245_gakekuzure⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{注意|ちゅうい}→注意：01464_chuui⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。

notes:
{崖|がけ} refers to a steep, often vertical rock face — a cliff or precipice. It can describe coastal cliffs, mountain faces, or any steep drop-off.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- ⟦{崖|がけ}っぷち→崖っぷち：16343_gakeppuchi⟧: cliff edge, brink
- ⟦{崖崩|がけくず}れ→崖崩れ：20245_gakekuzure⟧: cliff collapse, landslide
- {崖|がけ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{上|うえ}→上：00682_ue⟧: top of a cliff
- {崖|がけ}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{落|お}ちる→落ちる：01242_ochiru⟧: to fall from a cliff

USAGE:
⟦{崖|がけ}っぷち→崖っぷち：16343_gakeppuchi⟧ is very commonly used figuratively to mean 'on the brink' or 'in a desperate situation': ⟦{崖|がけ}っぷち→崖っぷち：16343_gakeppuchi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{立|た}たされる→立つ：00758_tatsu⟧ (to be driven to the edge). Often seen in sports and business contexts.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{断崖|だんがい}→断崖：05039_dangai⟧: precipice, sheer cliff (more literary)
- ⟦{絶壁|ぜっぺき}→絶壁：16412_zeppeki⟧: sheer cliff, precipice (emphasizes vertical drop)
